items.title: Report out on Closed Session from January 20, 2023

publicComments.name: Peter Cohen
publicComments.summary: Thanked the district for correcting enrollment snafus and encouraged the district to expand immersion programs to meet the California Department of Education's bilingual proficiency goal and to provide TK for immersion students.

publicComments.name: Alexis Betts
publicComments.summary: Advocated for accommodating all families who want to enroll in the Mandarin Immersion Program to build a healthier, sustainable program through 8th grade.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about underserved families at Orion not receiving adequate support and asked the district to consider a different structure, and also urged the district to apply for the TCLP program.

publicComments.name: William Dennis
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for sibling priority in school enrollment so his daughter could attend the same school as her brother.

publicComments.name: Deepika Germany (speaker: husband)
publicComments.summary: Advocated for an additional TK class in the Mandarin Immersion Program as his daughter is currently on the waitlist.

publicComments.name: Tina Taratutin Chung
publicComments.summary: Advocated for additional Mandarin Immersion classes to benefit more students including her son.

publicComments.name: Brandy Lee
publicComments.summary: Advocated for continued expansion of the Mandarin Immersion Program, citing strong academic data and the importance of bilingual education for her daughter.

publicComments.name: Jackie Chen
publicComments.summary: Described the difficult waitlist experience for the Mandarin Immersion Program and recommended 2 TK MI classes and 3 kindergarten MI classes.

publicComments.name: Julia Selesniba
publicComments.summary: Praised the academic rigor of the Mandarin Immersion Program and advocated for expanding both the kindergarten and TK programs.

publicComments.name: Alex Oh
publicComments.summary: Advocated for expansion of the TK and kindergarten Mandarin Immersion programs, citing the personal benefits of bilingual education.

publicComments.name: Angela Kang
publicComments.summary: Advocated for additional MI TK classes so that all interested parents, including herself, can have the opportunity to enroll their children.

publicComments.name: Sam Christianson
publicComments.summary: Expressed that the Mandarin Immersion Program is her family's only desired option and advocated for expanding the TK program.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about fairness in the lottery system, specifically regarding Odyssey Preschool preference and TK sibling preference, and asked the district to reform the lottery or add more classes.

publicComments.name: Jasper Chen
publicComments.summary: Encouraged the district to invest in expanding the Mandarin Immersion Program, citing the community benefits of a larger, thriving program.

publicComments.name: Anna Lee Maraz
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish about challenges faced by low-income and multilingual families in the Mandarin Immersion Program and requested more district support for those students.

publicComments.name: Keith Simmons
publicComments.summary: Asked the board to extend sibling priority to TK, expand MI to 2 TK classes and 3 kindergarten classes, and consider Adelante's waitlist as well.

publicComments.name: Heather Stamper
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for expanding TK and K MI classrooms to create a stable base and sustain the program through middle and high school.

publicComments.name: Mele Rosario
publicComments.summary: Asked for more funding and support for students with learning disabilities in the Mandarin Immersion Program, including resource teachers and aides in Mandarin.

publicComments.name: Richard Pond
publicComments.summary: Shared his family's positive experience with the Mandarin Immersion Program and hoped for expansion so more families could benefit.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker (Micah/Lau)
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for expansion of TK and kindergarten MI enrollment after his twin boys were successfully admitted off the waitlist.

publicComments.name: Sarah Rutherford
publicComments.summary: Asked for consistency between sibling policy for TK and the rest of the grades, particularly given the rollout of universal TK.

publicComments.name: Tiffany Chow
publicComments.summary: Explained that she moved to Redwood City specifically for the Mandarin Immersion Program and urged the district to expand kindergarten and TK enrollment.

publicComments.name: Strong Yin (speaker: Sean Yen)
publicComments.summary: Expressed interest in expanding the Mandarin Immersion Program and asked the board to guide the community on how they can help move the expansion forward.

publicComments.name: Julia Feng
publicComments.summary: Argued that the district should not artificially cap school demand and noted that immersion learners have only one or two windows to join the program.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker (Doshi)
publicComments.summary: Advocated for adding a TK MI class, noting that between preschool and sibling preferences there was little chance for his daughter to gain admission through the lottery.

publicComments.name: Philip Guy
publicComments.summary: Asked the board to expand the Mandarin Immersion Program in every way possible and invited the community to help make it happen.

publicComments.name: Omar Villanueva
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish asking for more support for Latino families in the Mandarin Immersion Program and requested removal of barriers to tutoring services within the school.

publicComments.name: Kyle Zipes
publicComments.summary: Argued that the lottery system is unacceptable and every family that wants to attend the MI school should be accommodated, suggesting the program may need its own campus.

publicComments.name: Ileana Harrison
publicComments.summary: Expressed excitement about the MI program growing and requested 2 TK classes and 3 kindergarten classes.
